summary: Sodo Mori is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kogen Mizuno and at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and G. P. Malalasekera, later serving as professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji from 1949 to 1957 under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Eko Hashimoto.
Soen Nakagawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, and trained under Gempo Yamamoto between approximately 1931 and 1961.

Sogen Omori worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Nihon University and under Jirokichi Yamada, Seisetsu Seki, and Bokuo Seki, later serving as professor (1970) and president (1978–1982) at Hanazono University.

Sogyal Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge, and under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Soiku Shigematsu specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Kyoto University, later holding posts at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).
Sojo Hirano was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and later held a post at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).

Sokatsu Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kosen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893–1898), later founding Tokyo Ryobokai (1901), the Ryobokai Dojo of North America (1906), and Ningen Zen Kyodan.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tokyo Fine Arts School, California School of Design, and under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku. He founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1930.

Sokichi Tsuda worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at Tokyo Senmon Gakko and held posts at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1914), Waseda University (~1918–1940), and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923).

Soko Morinaga worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Toyama High School and Daitoku-ji under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto, later serving as abbot at Daishuin (~1963–1995) and head of Hanazono University (1986–1994).

Sokuo Eto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and as professor at Komazawa University (1953).

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and as a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).
Soma Thera was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied at St. Benedict's College in Colombo and under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936.

Somadeva Vasudeva specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later serving as a professor at Kyoto University (2011) and as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit at Columbia University.

Somboon Watana works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Panjab University (1999) under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and is an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara, where he served as abbot (~1961–2013). He also led Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961).

Sonam Chhoki is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a PhD at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Choden works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She is a doctoral local researcher and project staff member (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
